newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek boost from firmer dollar.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek boost from firmer dollar.

text.p: German shares sought to get a boost from the firmer dollar in late dealings on Tuesday as prospects for and end to the Bundesbank-Bonn fight over the revaluation of gold reserves may soon come to an end.
The 30-share DAX index ended the session up 20.12 points at 3,625.74 points. The index rose to 3,631 points in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings.

The bourse got a late boost from statements from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer and Finance Minister Theo Waigel after a meeting in Bonn that they were on the way to finding an end to their dispute over Bonn's plans to revalue the reserves.
Waigel wants to use the booked profits from the reserves to pay down Germany's debt in a bid to help shore up Bonn's finances and qualify for European monetary union (EMU).
But traders said volumes were low, an indication of investor indecision about the future of the single currency and the risk it may be delayed from its January 1999 start date.
Those uncertainities are slowing the advance of German debt market prices, which has capped the share market's advance.
"The dollar is helping the market to gain some footing," said one Frankfurt trader. "But some are still sceptical as to how the Bundesbank fight with Bonn will impact EMU."

Construction group shares were at the forefront of activity on Tuesday after builder Hochtief AG and commercial bank Deutsche Bank AG said on Monday they were giving up plans to pool their stake in construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG.
The plan was dropped after the European Commission said it would pass the case on to German cartel authorities.
Holzmann shares tumbled 17 marks at 491 marks, while Hochtief shares fell 90 pfennigs at 73.80 marks. Deutsche shares lost 12 pfennigs to 96.38 marks.
